Post-DRM Distribution History: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition

The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition, officially released on October 28, 2016, by Bethesda Softworks, was distributed primarily through Valve's Steam platform. This distribution relied on Steam's integrated digital rights management (DRM) and authentication system. This section documents the initial circumvention of this DRM and the subsequent distribution within the warez scene.

Release Name: The primary release was titled The.Elder.Scrolls.V.Skyrim.Special.Edition-???.
Release Date: This release appeared on October 27, 2016, one day prior to the game's official Steam release date. This pre-release timing is characteristic of scene groups leveraging pre-load files or early access.
Distribution Channels: Initial distribution of the ??? release occurred via private, invite-only File Transfer Protocol (FTP) servers, commonly known as "topsites," which serve as the primary distribution hubs within the warez scene. From these topsites, the release rapidly propagated to public-facing distribution channels, including various torrent indexing sites (e.g., The Pirate Bay, RuTracker, 1337x) and direct download (DDL) hosters.
2. DRM and Circumvention Method
Original DRM: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition, as distributed via Steam, relied exclusively on Steam's native DRM and authentication system. It is crucial to note that, unlike many other AAA titles released around this period, Skyrim Special Edition did not incorporate third-party anti-tamper solutions such as Denuvo Anti-Tamper at its initial launch.
Circumvention Technique: The ??? release circumvented Steam's DRM through a Steam API emulation and executable patching technique. This method involved:
Executable Modification: The game's primary executable, SkyrimSE.exe, was patched to bypass or redirect calls to the Steam API functions responsible for ownership verification and authentication checks.
Steam API Emulation: A custom steam_api64.dll (or a similar Steam API library replacement) was included in the crack. This modified DLL intercepted legitimate Steam API calls (e.g., SteamAPI_Init, SteamAPI_IsSubscribedApp) and returned pre-determined success values, effectively simulating a valid Steam session without requiring an active Steam client, a legitimate game license, or connection to Steam servers. This allowed the game to launch and function offline, independent of Steam's services.
3. Standard Installation Sequence (Scene Release)

The typical installation process for the ??? release of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition involved the following steps:

Acquisition: The user would download the release package, which was commonly distributed as an ISO image file (e.g., ???-the.elder.scrolls.v.skyrim.special.edition.iso) or a series of compressed archives (e.g., RAR files).
Mount/Extraction:
If an ISO image, the user would mount it using a virtual drive utility (e.g., Daemon Tools Lite, Alcohol 120%, or Windows' built-in ISO mounter).
If compressed archives, the user would extract all files to a designated temporary folder using an archiving tool (e.g., WinRAR, 7-Zip).
Setup Execution: The user would navigate to the mounted virtual drive or extracted folder and execute the setup.exe installer provided by ???.
Installation: The user would follow the on-screen prompts of the ??? installer, which typically involved selecting an installation directory, agreeing to terms, and waiting for the game files to be copied to the hard drive.
Crack Application: Upon completion of the main installation, the user would locate the "???" or "Crack" folder within the mounted ISO or extracted files. All contents from this folder (typically including SkyrimSE.exe and steam_api64.dll) would then be copied into the game's primary installation directory, overwriting any existing files when prompted.
Launch: The game would then be launched by executing SkyrimSE.exe directly from its installation directory, bypassing the need for Steam.
